description.en: Turkey observes a mix of national and regional public holidays that reflect its history, culture, and traditions. These holidays influence work schedules, school terms, travel plans, and the availability of public services.

sections.title: About Turkey
sections.content: Turkey is a sovereign state with a rich cultural heritage. Its public holidays are an important part of the national identity, bringing together communities to celebrate historical milestones, religious festivals, and cultural traditions. The official language and local customs play a significant role in how these days are observed.

sections.title: How Public Holidays Are Observed in Turkey
sections.content: On most public holidays in Turkey, government offices, schools, and banks are closed. Many private businesses also close or operate on reduced hours, allowing citizens to spend time with family and participate in local celebrations.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Turkey?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Turkey?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Turkey?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Turkey?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Turkey?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
